index.title: QoreDB compared
index.subtitle: Side-by-side comparisons with the database clients developers use most. Facts come from each vendor's website and documentation, with sources and the date they were checked.

page.cta_body: The Core edition is free and open source. Install it alongside your current client and compare on your own databases.

qoredb.price: Core is free. Pro is a one-time payment of {{proPrice}}.
qoredb.technology: Rust and Tauri, using the system WebView
qoredb.databases: {{count}} databases in the free Core, including MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery and Elasticsearch
qoredb.telemetry: None. Only an update check against GitHub, which can be turned off.
qoredb.safety: Environment tags. On production connections, DROP and TRUNCATE are blocked, DELETE asks for confirmation and ALTER shows a warning. Read-only mode. Custom rules in Pro.
qoredb.ai: Read-only MCP server in Core. Database Agent in Pro, with 7 providers or Qore AI Local.
qoredb.notebooks: SQL, MongoDB and Markdown notebooks in Core, saved as .qnb files

dbeaver.description: QoreDB vs DBeaver: license, price, supported databases, telemetry, production safety and AI, compared with sources.
dbeaver.intro: DBeaver is one of the most widely used database clients. Its Community edition is open source and connects to a very large number of databases through JDBC and ODBC drivers. QoreDB takes a different route: a Rust application with native drivers for {{count}} databases, including the NoSQL ones, in its free edition.

values.price: Community is free. PRO from $113 per year (Lite), $255 (Enterprise) or $510 (Ultimate).
values.technology: Java on Eclipse RCP, with a bundled OpenJDK
values.databases: 100+ through JDBC and ODBC. Community covers ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake, BigQuery and Elasticsearch. MongoDB, Redis and Cassandra require a PRO edition.
values.telemetry: Anonymous usage statistics, which can be turned off in Preferences.
values.safety: Connection types (development, test, production) with confirmation before SQL execution or data changes. Read-only connections.
values.ai: AI chat with OpenAI or GitHub Copilot in Community. More providers in PRO.

stronger.title: Far more databases
stronger.body: Through JDBC and ODBC, DBeaver reaches well over a hundred databases, including Oracle, Db2 and Redshift, which QoreDB does not support.

stronger.title: Detailed connection restrictions
stronger.body: Each connection type can require confirmation for SQL execution and for data edits separately, on top of read-only connections.

stronger.title: A long track record
stronger.body: More than a decade of releases, a large community and extensive documentation.

different.title: NoSQL in the free edition
different.body: MongoDB, Redis and Cassandra are part of the free Apache-2.0 Core. In DBeaver, they require a PRO edition.

different.title: No Java runtime
different.body: QoreDB is written in Rust and renders its interface with the system WebView. There is no JVM to bundle or tune.

different.title: Statement-level production rules
different.body: QoreDB parses each statement: on production connections it blocks DROP and TRUNCATE, asks to confirm DELETE and warns on ALTER.

switch: QoreDB does not import DBeaver connection settings. To move a connection, copy its URL and paste it into the QoreDB connection form, which detects the driver and fills in the fields.
Saved scripts can be pasted into the query editor or into a notebook. Both tools can run side by side while you switch.

tableplus.description: QoreDB vs TablePlus: license, price, supported databases, telemetry, production safety and AI, compared with sources.
tableplus.intro: TablePlus is a polished, proprietary database client with a native interface on each platform. It offers a limited free trial and a one-time license. QoreDB is open source: its Core edition has no tab or window limits and includes {{count}} databases.

values.price: Free trial limited to 2 tabs, 2 windows and 2 filters. Basic license $99 one-time for 1 device with 1 year of updates, then $59 to renew updates.
values.technology: Native app on each platform (the Windows version runs on .NET Framework 4.8)
values.databases: About 23, including Redis, MongoDB, Cassandra, ClickHouse, BigQuery, Snowflake, DuckDB and Elasticsearch
values.telemetry: Anonymous crash reports. Turning them off requires a license.
values.safety: Safe Mode with several levels, up to asking for a password before running queries. Connection tags such as production.
values.ai: AI assistant with your own provider. MCP server documented for macOS.

stronger.title: Native interface
stronger.body: TablePlus uses each operating system's own UI toolkit rather than a web view.

stronger.title: iOS app
stronger.body: TablePlus also runs on iPhone and iPad. QoreDB is desktop only.

stronger.title: Granular Safe Mode
stronger.body: Safe Mode can require a password or a confirmation before queries run, configurable per connection.

different.title: Open source and free to use
different.body: The Core edition is Apache-2.0, with no limits on tabs, windows or filters, for personal and commercial use.

different.title: No telemetry at all
different.body: QoreDB sends no usage or crash data. There is nothing to turn off and no license required to do it.

different.title: Notebooks and production rules
different.body: SQL and MongoDB notebooks are part of Core, and production connections block destructive statements by default.

switch: QoreDB does not import TablePlus connections. To move a connection, copy its URL and paste it into the QoreDB connection form, which detects the driver and fills in the fields.
Saved queries can be pasted into the query editor or into a notebook. Both tools can run side by side while you switch.

datagrip.description: QoreDB vs DataGrip: license, price, supported databases, telemetry, production safety and AI, compared with sources.
datagrip.intro: DataGrip is JetBrains' database IDE, built on the IntelliJ platform. It is known for its SQL editing tools and is free for non-commercial use, with a subscription otherwise. QoreDB's Core edition is free for any use, including at work, and its Pro edition is a one-time payment.

values.price: Free for non-commercial individual use. Individual license €109 for the first year, then €87 and €65. Organizations: €259 per user per year. Prices excluding VAT.
values.technology: IntelliJ platform on the JetBrains Runtime (Java)
values.databases: More than 50, including MongoDB, Redis, Cassandra, ClickHouse, DuckDB, Snowflake and BigQuery. Elasticsearch support is basic.
values.telemetry: Off by default with a paid license, except error reports. Required with the free non-commercial license.
values.safety: Read-only data sources and a color per data source.
values.ai: AI agents and an MCP server, with your own key or JetBrains AI.
values.notebooks: Only through the Zeppelin plugin, whose development is suspended

stronger.title: IDE-grade SQL editing
stronger.body: Context-aware completion, refactoring, code inspections and navigation across schemas, built on years of IntelliJ work.

stronger.title: Part of the JetBrains ecosystem
stronger.body: The same database tools are built into other JetBrains IDEs such as IntelliJ IDEA.

stronger.title: More databases
stronger.body: More than 50 databases are supported, including some that QoreDB does not cover, such as Oracle and Db2.

different.title: Free for commercial use
different.body: The Core edition is Apache-2.0 and free at work too. Pro is a one-time payment instead of a yearly subscription.

different.title: No telemetry on any edition
different.body: QoreDB sends no usage data, whatever edition or license you use.

different.title: Notebooks built in
different.body: SQL, MongoDB and Markdown notebooks are part of Core, saved as plain .qnb files.

switch: QoreDB does not import DataGrip data sources. To move a connection, copy its URL and paste it into the QoreDB connection form, which detects the driver and fills in the fields.
Scratch files and saved queries can be pasted into the query editor or into a notebook. Both tools can run side by side while you switch.

beekeeper-studio.description: QoreDB vs Beekeeper Studio: license, price, supported databases, telemetry, production safety and AI, compared with sources.
beekeeper-studio.intro: Beekeeper Studio is a friendly, open source SQL client with a GPL Community edition and paid plans that unlock more databases and features. QoreDB includes all of its {{count}} databases in the free Core edition, under the Apache-2.0 license.

values.price: Community is free. Paid plans from $9 per month billed yearly (Indie), $14 (Professional) or $18 (Business).
values.databases: Free: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite, SQL Server, CockroachDB, TiDB, Redshift, BigQuery, Redis and more. DuckDB and Cassandra from Indie, ClickHouse and MongoDB from Professional, Snowflake on Business. Elasticsearch not listed.
values.safety: Read-only mode (free since version 6.1) and connection colors.
values.ai: AI Shell with your own key, in paid plans.

stronger.title: Simple, approachable interface
stronger.body: Beekeeper Studio focuses on a clean, easy to learn interface for everyday SQL work.

stronger.title: Redshift support
stronger.body: Amazon Redshift is available in the free edition. QoreDB does not support it.

different.title: Every database in the free edition
different.body: ClickHouse, MongoDB, DuckDB, Cassandra, Snowflake and Elasticsearch are part of the free Core. In Beekeeper Studio, several of them need a paid plan.

different.title: Permissive license
different.body: Core is Apache-2.0 rather than GPL, and Pro is a one-time payment rather than a subscription.

different.title: Rust instead of Electron
different.body: QoreDB runs on Tauri with the system WebView, without shipping its own copy of Chromium.

switch: QoreDB does not import Beekeeper Studio connections. To move a connection, copy its URL and paste it into the QoreDB connection form, which detects the driver and fills in the fields.
Saved queries can be pasted into the query editor or into a notebook. Both tools can run side by side while you switch.

pgadmin.description: QoreDB vs pgAdmin: license, price, supported databases, telemetry, production safety and AI, compared with sources.
pgadmin.intro: pgAdmin is a long-standing open source project focused on PostgreSQL administration, available as a desktop app or a web server. QoreDB is a general database client: it works with PostgreSQL and {{others}} other databases in the same window.

values.platforms: Windows, macOS, Linux, plus a server mode used from a browser
values.technology: Python (Flask) and React, in an Electron shell for the desktop app
values.telemetry: No usage statistics found. An update check is on by default.
values.safety: A color per server. No read-only mode found in the documentation.
values.ai: Free AI assistant and reports with your own provider.

stronger.title: Deep PostgreSQL administration
stronger.body: Backup and restore, maintenance tasks, pgAgent jobs, a PL/pgSQL debugger and schema diff, all dedicated to PostgreSQL.

stronger.title: Multi-user web deployment
stronger.body: pgAdmin can run as a web application shared by a team, with its own user accounts.

stronger.title: Free AI features
stronger.body: The AI assistant works with your own provider at no cost. In QoreDB, the Database Agent is part of Pro.

different.title: Beyond PostgreSQL
different.body: One app for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, ClickHouse, DuckDB and {{count}} databases in total.

different.title: Production guardrails
different.body: Read-only mode, and production connections that block DROP and TRUNCATE and ask to confirm DELETE.

different.title: Notebooks
different.body: Mix SQL and Markdown in notebooks, saved as plain .qnb files you can share.

switch: QoreDB does not import pgAdmin server exports. To move a server, copy its connection URL and paste it into the QoreDB connection form, which detects the driver and fills in the fields.
For administration tasks such as pgAgent jobs or the debugger, you can keep pgAdmin next to QoreDB.
